page: Amazon Web Services r7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute instance designed for demanding in-memory workloads. It runs on AMD EPYC 9R14 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware delivers 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs on dedicated silicon with single threading per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI, paired with 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core. It is configured with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing a consistent 1:8 core-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The platform includes a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and high-speed memory subsystems. In computational testing, the server achieved a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 592,711.09 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 21,229.0, backed by strong single-core results (2,031.0 in Geekbench and 3,094.47 in stress-ng). Memory bandwidth reached 652.59 GB/sec on uncached 256MB read operations and 309.09 GB/sec on writes. Key application tests highlight outstanding throughput, logging 332.38 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and top-tier PassMark metrics across extended instructions (302,965.71) and encryption (242,744.52). While LLM prompt ingestion achieves top-tier results across small, medium, and 70B models, CPU-bound generation speeds register lower, such as 4.64 tokens/sec on 70B models.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the r7a.metal-48xl consolidates massive computing resources and DDR5 memory density onto a single bare-metal chassis without hypervisor overhead. A key operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage disks, necessitating external storage configurations for persistent state. The instance represents an efficient scale-up solution for large memory footprints, enterprise in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis clusters, big data analytics, complex Clang compilations, and high-concurrency memory-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance featuring 192 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 cores (x86_64 at 3.7 GHz) and 1536.0 GB of DDR5-5000 RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Built without hypervisor overhead, it includes 50 Gbps baseline networking, no GPUs, and no bundled local storage. Benchmarks place the system in the top tier for multi-core compute (stress-ng multi-core 592,711.09, Geekbench 21,229.0) and uncached memory bandwidth (652.59 GB/sec read, 309.09 GB/sec write). It excels in in-memory transaction performance, executing 332.38 million Redis SET operations per second alongside top-tier encryption and compiler metrics. Tradeoffs include reliance on external block storage and average sequential LLM generation speeds. It is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise analytics, high-density caching layers, and high-parallelism memory-intensive workloads.
